newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Albanians on looting spree demolish border posts.
newsitem.headline: Albanians on looting spree demolish border posts.

text.p: Albanian rebels looted government property in the north of their country and devastated border posts as government troops and police fled in disarray, witnesses said on Saturday.
"The other side of the border is in complete chaos. The rule of law has collapsed," a Macedonian border guard commander told Reuters at the St Naum crossing.
Some one hundred metres (yards) away, the abandoned Albanian border post was demolished, its doors and windows gutted. Even the Albanian red flag with its double-headed eagle was gone.
"Non-governmental forces even took the window sills away," the officer said.

Non-governmental forces is the name given by the Macedonian army to the Albanian rebels who embarked on a looting spree earlier this week after the armed revolt over failed savings schemes spread to the north of the country.
The few refugees who made it across the border said the rebels had tanks in their possession after army and police fled, leaving all their equipment behind.

"The army and police in this region were caught between a rock and a hard place. They had seen they could not fight it out with the rebels or had no desire to, they had nowhere to go and we suppose their lives were spared in return for the hardware and equipment," another Macedonian officer said.
Gunfire, chiefly from small arms, could be heard in the distance throughout the day, shattering the tranquility of the mountains dominating crystal clear Lake Ohrid, shared by Macedonia and Albania.

Spartak and Lindita Caja were the only refugees from Albania to cross on Saturday and it took them almost twelve hours to make the 100 km (60 mile) journey from Tirana where they had an upholstery shop.
"Too many checkpoints on the road," Lindita said. "Too many armed men, ready to steal and loot."

The family of six, including three daughters and a garndmother, on their way to the nearest airport to board a plane for New York, made it across in their car, but other foreigners in the area were not so lucky.
Rebels stripped their foreign victims to their underwear and forces them to walk to the Macedonian border barefoot, witnesses said.
"So far we know about some Turkish businessmen and Italian and German journalists who suffered that fate," one said. "One Turk lost $50,000 and now the rebels see all foreigners as walking jackpots."
Four Catholic nuns from the Dushai Ferzi monastery in northern Albania arrived in the Yugoslav republic of Montenegro early on Saturday, telling a harrowing tale of anarchy.
"Our cars were robbed and two of our sisters were held captive for six hours. We were very scared," Lusia Cuplie, a sister of the order, told Reuters.

As the evacuation of foreign nationals from Albania got into full swing, six helicopters from NATO forces in Bosnia landed late on Friday in the Montenegrin capital of Podgorica, unloading 89 foreigners, incuding 18 diplomats and their families, but also some 40 unwelcome companions - armed Albanians who forced their way on board.
They were now in Podgorica prison, undergoing investigation, Montenegrin Interior Minister Filip Vujinovic told reporters.

Macedonian guards patrolled the sealed border in full combat gear and their Yugoslav colleagues even used armoured personnel carriers, but security officials from both countries feared armed incursions in the future.
"So far so good. But what when the food they have looted runs out? The only place they can find it is here," a Macedonian border guard said.
